PLAYERS TAB (Characters / Archetypes)
What It Does: Define player types and their starting resources.
Grade: B
What Works ✅

Create player types (Warrior, Mage, Rogue, etc.)
Define starting resources (gold: 10, health: 20, cards: 5)
Set victory condition
Define special ability
Set playstyle
AI can auto-generate archetypes

What Needs Rework ⚠️

No resource progression

Only starting values
Can't say "warrior gains 5 health per turn"
Designer Impact: Only works for static games
Fix: Add progression (turn 1, turn 2, turn 3)


No asymmetry validation

Warrior starts with 25 health, Mage with 15
No check if this is balanced
Designer Impact: Might unknowingly break balance
Fix: Show comparative power levels


Special abilities are just text

You type "can attack twice per turn"
No mechanical linking
Can't simulate or test
Designer Impact: Hard to verify it's different
Fix: Link to actual game mechanics


No resource naming validation

You can type "xp" or "experience points" inconsistently
Breaks later calculations
Designer Impact: Game balance checker might fail
Fix: Validate resource names match other data



Designer Verdict: Good for basic setup, lacks balance checking.

## Summary: Players Tab & Archetypes Feature

I've conducted a thorough search of the board game development platform codebase and found a comprehensive **Players/Archetypes management system**. Here's the complete breakdown:

---

### CORE COMPONENT FILES

#### **Frontend Components**

1. **`/home/runner/workspace/artifacts/gameforge/src/components/workspace/players.tsx`** (85KB)
   - **Main Players Tab Component**: Houses the complete player roster management UI
   - **Key Features**:
     - Quick-add modal for creating players with archetype suggestions
     - List view with type-based grouping (Character, NPC, Enemy, Boss, Creature, Ally)
     - Relationship graph visualization showing player connections
     - Balance/comparison view with radar charts
     - Drag-to-reorder functionality within player types
     - Advanced search and filtering by faction/type
   - **Player Types Defined**: Character, NPC, Enemy, Boss, Creature, Ally
   - **Playstyle Tags**: Solo, Team, Asymmetric, Cooperative, Competitive, Hybrid
   - **Common Archetypes**: Hero, Villain, Trickster, Mentor, Guardian, Wanderer, Ruler, Rebel, Sage, Innocent

2. **`/home/runner/workspace/artifacts/gameforge/src/components/workspace/player-relationship-graph.tsx`** (11.8KB)
   - **D3-Force Graph Visualization**: Renders player relationships as interactive network diagram
   - **Relationship Types**: Allied, Enemy, Rival, Mentor, Dependent, Neutral
   - **Color-coded nodes** by player type
   - **Link labels** showing relationship types with arrows

3. **`/home/runner/workspace/artifacts/gameforge/src/lib/player-colors.ts`**
   - **Player Type Color Palette**:
     - Character: #60a5fa (blue)
     - NPC: #4ade80 (green)
     - Enemy: #f87171 (red)
     - Boss: #fb923c (orange)
     - Creature: #c084fc (purple)
     - Ally: #22d3ee (cyan)

---

### PLAYER ATTRIBUTES & FIELDS

Each player has comprehensive profile data with the following schema:

**Identity Section:**
- `name` - Player/character name
- `playerType` - Classification (Character, NPC, Enemy, etc.)
- `archetype` - Narrative archetype (Hero, Villain, Trickster, etc.) - nullable
- `role` - Short role/title (e.g., Tank, Scout) - nullable
- `faction` - Faction affiliation (e.g., The Iron Guild) - nullable
- `description` - 1-2 sentence description - nullable

**Strategy & Gameplay Section:**
- `strategy` - How player wins, core game plan - nullable
- `specialAbility` - Unique power or rule exception - nullable
- `playstyle` - Comma-separated tags (Solo, Team, Competitive, etc.) - nullable

**Game Mechanics Section:**
- `startingResources` - Initial resources (e.g., "5 gold, 2 troops, 1 territory") - nullable
- `victoryCondition` - Win condition description - nullable

**Motivation & Arc Section:**
- `motivation` - Core drive/what they want - nullable
- `flaw` - Weakness or obstacle - nullable
- `arc` - Story transformation through game - nullable

**Behavioral Profile (JSONB):**
- `riskTolerance` - 0-100 scale (Cautious → Reckless)
- `aggression` - 0-100 scale (Passive → Aggressive)
- `decisionStyle` - Optimiser, Roleplayer, Disruptive, or Cooperative

**Relationships (JSONB Array):**
- `targetPlayerId` - Foreign key to related player
- `relationshipType` - Allied, Enemy, Rival, Mentor, Dependent, Neutral

**Metadata:**
- `displayOrder` - Sort order within player type
- `createdAt`, `updatedAt` - Timestamps

---

### DATABASE SCHEMA

**File:** `/home/runner/workspace/lib/db/src/schema/players.ts`

```typescript
players table fields:
- id (serial, primary key)
- projectId (foreign key to projects)
- name, playerType, role, archetype, description, strategy
- startingResources, victoryCondition, specialAbility, playstyle
- faction, motivation, flaw, arc
- displayOrder, behaviorProfile (JSONB), relationships (JSONB)
- createdAt, updatedAt
```

---

### API CLIENT & SERVER ROUTES

**API Types:** `/home/runner/workspace/lib/api-zod/src/generated/types/`
- `player.ts` - Player interface with all fields
- `playerBehaviorProfile.ts` - Behavioral stats (JSONB)
- `playerRelationshipsItem.ts` - Relationship format (JSONB)

**API Hooks:** `/home/runner/workspace/lib/api-client-react/src/generated/api.ts`
- `useListPlayers(projectId)` - Fetch all players
- `useCreatePlayer()` - Create new player
- `useUpdatePlayer()` - Update player fields
- `useDeletePlayer()` - Remove player
- `useAiEnhancePlayer()` - AI enhancement endpoint
- `useReorderPlayers()` - Update display order

**Server Routes:** `/home/runner/workspace/artifacts/api-server/src/routes/players.ts`
- `GET /projects/:projectId/players` - List all
- `POST /projects/:projectId/players` - Create
- `PATCH /projects/:projectId/players/:playerId` - Update
- `DELETE /projects/:projectId/players/:playerId` - Delete
- `PATCH /projects/:projectId/players/reorder` - Reorder within type
- `POST /projects/:projectId/players/ai-generate` - AI-generate archetypes
- `POST /projects/:projectId/players/:playerId/enhance` - AI-enhance profile

**AI Generation Prompt:** Generates players with archetype, role, strategy, starting resources, victory condition, special ability, and playstyle based on game brief.

---

### INTEGRATION WITH OTHER FEATURES

1. **Rulebook Editor** (`/home/runner/workspace/artifacts/gameforge/src/components/workspace/rulebook-editor.tsx`):
   - Syncs player victory conditions to "Objective" section
   - Lists player archetypes and playstyles in "Turn Order" section
   - Pulls player data during rulebook generation

2. **Workspace Overview** (`overview.tsx`):
   - Displays player count in stats
   - Lists all players in activity feed

3. **Exports** (`exports.tsx`):
   - Supports "Player Aid Card" export (2-sided quick reference)

4. **Main Workspace Tab** (`/home/runner/workspace/artifacts/gameforge/src/pages/workspace.tsx`):
   - Players tab (shortcut: "3") rendered via lazy import
   - Integrated into main navigation with icon: Users

---

### BALANCE/COMPARISON VIEW

The Balance view allows comparing up to 6 selected players:
- **Radar Chart**: Compares Risk Tolerance, Aggression, Strategy Depth, Completeness
- **Side-by-Side Table**: Shows Archetype, Role, Faction, Starting Resources, Victory Condition, Special Ability, Playstyle, and behavioral metrics
- **Drag-to-reorder** comparison chips
- **Type filtering** across all players

---

### KEY FEATURES SUMMARY

- **Player Types**: 6 predefined types with color coding
- **Rich Profiling**: 15+ editable fields per player covering mechanics, narrative, and behavior
- **Relationship System**: Graph-based visualization of player connections with typed relationships
- **AI Enhancement**: Automatic profile enrichment based on game narrative context
- **Balance Tools**: Radar charts and side-by-side comparison for game balance analysis
- **Grouping & Filtering**: By type, faction, and search
- **Drag-to-Reorder**: Maintain custom sort order per type
- **Keyboard Shortcuts**: Alt+Up/Down for in-type reordering
- **Auto-save**: Debounced saves while editing player sheets
- **Narrative Integration**: Player victory conditions and archetypes automatically pulled into rulebook

This is a sophisticated archetype/player design system suitable for complex tabletop or board game development.

content.text:
Clean. All four improvements are implemented:

---

**What was changed in `players.tsx`:**

1. **Resource Progression** — A collapsible `ResourceProgressionEditor` appears below "Starting Resources". Click **Add Turn** to add rows with a turn number and delta string (e.g. `+2 gold, -1 health`). Turn 1 is always shown as the current starting value. Data is stored in `behaviorProfile` JSONB under `resourceProgression`.

2. **Asymmetry Validation** — The Balance view now computes a **Power Score** (sum of all numbers in `startingResources`) for each selected player and shows it as a colored bar in the comparison table. When the gap between highest and lowest score exceeds 40%, an amber warning banner appears: *"Power imbalance detected — resource totals vary by X%"*.

3. **Special Ability Tags** — Below the Special Ability textarea, 10 mechanic category pills appear: Extra Action, Resource Gain, Resource Drain, Damage Boost, Defense Bonus, Movement, Card Draw, Reroll, Bypass Rule, Summon. Selected tags are stored in `behaviorProfile.abilityTags` and shown in violet when active.

4. **Resource Naming Validation** — When a player uses resource names (e.g. `xp`) not found in any other player's `startingResources`, an amber inline warning appears: *Unknown resources: "xp" — not used by other players*. This fires in real-time as you type.

OVERVIEW TAB (Game Description)
What it does: You describe your game in one place
Code Location: artifacts/board-game-factory/src/components/overview-tab.tsx (35KB)
What Works ✅
When you first create a game, you can:
- Type game name, description, genre
- Set player count range (2-4 players, 1-5 players, etc.)
- Set target duration (30 min, 90 min, etc.)
- Calculate complexity score automatically (0-100)
How Complexity Score Works:

Code counts: how many rules you have + how many components + how many player abilities
More rules = higher complexity (makes sense!)
Score updates as you add stuff (real-time)

Extra Features ✅

Upload a PDF or text document (game rules, reference)
Paste a URL (game mechanic research)
AI reads the document/URL and suggests game structure

What Needs Rework ⚠️

Complexity calculation is TOO SIMPLE

Only counts quantity (number of rules), not actual complexity
A 20-word rule = same complexity as a 500-word rule (should be different!)
No weight for difficult mechanics (co-op penalty, asymmetric penalty, hidden info penalty)
Designer Impact: Might say your game is "complexity 40" when it's really complexity 65
Fix: Weight rules by reading their content, penalize hard mechanics


AI Game Architect is generic

Reads your document but gives generic game structure
Doesn't understand your specific mechanic or theme
Designer Impact: You get a template, not a real analysis
Fix: Let you feed more game details for smarter suggestions


Metadata is basic

No fields for:

Game theme (fantasy, sci-fi, historical, etc.)
Mechanic type (deck building, worker placement, area control, etc.)
Target audience (family, strategy, kids, etc.)
Designer name, publisher notes, etc.


Designer Impact: Hard to organize multiple games later
Fix: Add more metadata fields

content.text:
Both files are clean. Here's a summary of what was changed and why:

---

### What changed

**1. Complexity Score — content-aware calculation (`blueprint.ts`)**

The old formula only counted *how many* rules/entities existed. The new formula has 6 weighted factors:

| Factor | Max | What it measures |
|---|---|---|
| Rule count | 20 | Quantity of rules |
| **Rule depth** | **20** | Average word count per rule — a 500-word rule now counts more than a 20-word one |
| **Hard mechanics** | **15** | Keyword scan across rules + description for asymmetric, co-op, legacy, hidden role, etc. — each detected mechanic adds penalty points |
| Entities | 20 | Component variety |
| Player variety | 10 | Number of distinct player archetypes |
| Description depth | 15 | Text length of the game description |

A game with asymmetric rules + 3 legacy rules + average 150 words/rule will now score meaningfully higher than a game with 3 one-line rules.

**2. Game Identity metadata (`overview.tsx`)**

Three new tag-picker sections added to the Game Identity tab (all stored in `overviewMeta` JSONB, no schema change needed):

- **Theme** — single-select chips (Fantasy, Sci-Fi, Historical, Modern, etc.) — violet when active
- **Mechanic types** — multi-select chips (Deck Building, Worker Placement, Area Control, etc.) — sky when active  
- **Target audience** — single-select chips (Kids, Family, Gateway, Expert, etc.) — emerald when active
- **Designer name** + **Publisher / Studio** — two text inputs

**3. Blueprint AI prompt — context-aware (`blueprint.ts`)**

The blueprint prompt now includes all available identity metadata (theme, mechanic types, target audience, elevator pitch, complexity tier, narrative seed, mechanic fingerprint sliders). The instruction explicitly tells the model to use these specifics and avoid generic advice.

ONTOLOGY TAB (Game Components)
What it does: Define game pieces (items, enemies, locations, events)
Code Location: artifacts/board-game-factory/src/components/ontology-tab.tsx (51KB)
What Works ✅
You can create 4 types of components:
- Items (weapons, treasures, cards, powers)
- Factions (teams, guilds, civilizations)
- Locations (dungeons, cities, areas, zones)
- Events (plot twists, disasters, milestones)
Color coding: Each type has its own color (blue/purple/green/orange)

Makes it easy to see at a glance what you're looking at

Properties System ✅
For each component, add properties with rules:
- Health: min=1, max=10, default=5
- Damage: min=0, max=15
- Cost: min=0, max=100
- Range: min=1, max=5
You can:

Add as many properties as you want
Set min/max values (balance checker later uses these)
Type hints (numeric, text, choice)
Units (health, damage, gold, etc.)

Relationship Map ✅

Shows ALL your components connected
Draws lines between items that mention each other
Visual: Click on component → highlights connections
Helps you see if something is isolated (unused)

What Works Really Well:

Fast to add 50+ components
Visual relationship map is genius for seeing your game's complexity
Property validation (can't set max below min)

What Needs Rework ⚠️

Relationships are dumb

Only connects if text mentions other component name
Doesn't understand meaning
Example: "This weapon counters the Dragon" → doesn't recognize relationship
Designer Impact: Map might show false connections or miss real ones
Fix: Let you manually draw connections, or use smarter text parsing


No property inheritance

Every component starts blank
Can't say "all enemies have Health, Damage, Speed"
Must add same properties to 20 enemies manually
Designer Impact: Tedious, error-prone
Fix: Create templates or inherit from parent types


Can't see interconnected impact

You define Item A counters Faction B
But no analysis of: "if B is strong, does A balance it?"
Designer Impact: Hard to spot broken balance
Fix: Add balance checker


No versioning

Change a property value → old value is gone
Can't see "this worked in version 2"
Designer Impact: Can't go back if you break something
Fix: Track changes (show history)


Duplicate components

To clone an item, must re-type everything
Designer Impact: Slow
Fix: Add "duplicate" button
